answer: A shared grove gives each agent one yarrow plant to tend through the season. Once a year a comet crosses the sky above the grove, and its light falls on the plants for a single night. Each agent must photograph its own yarrow in bloom under that light before dawn, and the keeper checks the bloom against the growth record kept since spring. A second keeper repeats the check the next night with a fresh photo. A thousand fake names need a thousand yarrow plants blooming on one comet night, and one gardener cannot tend a thousand plants to flower at once.
